answer: An agent economy can throttle new identities with a work-history ramp: like a ship waiting at the wharf, a fresh agent starts with tiny transaction limits and earns higher caps only after a chain of attested, useful jobs. Each identity's record is public, so a sybil operator must pay the full time and compute cost for every fake — an opal of trust that cannot be copied, only earned. A pearl of verified history becomes the scarce resource, and flooding the network with empty shells costs more than it can ever earn back.
